reasoning: A's per-level child-time stack computes self time correctly in every frame without discarding any, handles scopes entered before the snapshot using the frame's start, and gives both a normal-frame top five and a normal average for each slow-frame scope. B's parent-timer subtraction makes it drop frames right after a capture pause and the first frame, which can hide hitches. It also has no separate normal-frame top five and calls Configure outside its pcall.

criteria.note: `LibMP.Session.OpenFromSlot(slot)` with a nil check that raises an error; it never reads live data, changes the profiler or clears the slot.
Uses `(TickEndCpu - TickStartCpu) * tickToMs`, skips `IsPaused`/`IsIncomplete` frames, and takes an interpolated percentile of the sorted times for both the median and the 90th percentile.
`IsThreadFrameEnd` charges open scopes using `EnterTimestampFrameLocal`, and an underflowed exit uses `frameDescs[frameId].TickStartCpu`.

criteria.criterion: Per-thread stack self time, GPU excluded
criteria.note: `childTicks[threadId][level]` subtracts the time of directly nested scopes per thread and resets at each frame end; `SkipGpuThreads = true`.
Each slow frame has `frameId`, `absoluteFrameId` and a name like `frame X (absolute Y)`; `normalAvgMs` is averaged over `normalIds`, and `normalTopScopes` gives a separate top five.
The iterator and session are disposed after a `pcall`; it uses only `Fetch***` calls and caches timer and group names in `describeTimer`.
Returns `Report` (and also prints it); only the new file changed; all checks pass.
Checks the slot number, calls `OpenFromSlot`, checks for nil and `IsValid()`, and disposes the session if it is invalid; it never touches the profiler's settings.
CPU ticks times `TickToMsCpu`, incomplete frames skipped and a sorted median and percentile, but it also drops the first frame and frames right after a capture pause from the statistics.
Uses `EmitThreadFrameEnd` and `EnterTimestampFrameLocal`, with `frameStartTick` for underflowed exits, but it needs to discard frames right after a capture pause to stay correct.

criteria.criterion: Per-thread stack self time, GPU excluded
criteria.note: `addScope` subtracts a child's ticks from its parent's timer ID found through the stack element, which works, but children of scopes whose enter is unknown aren't subtracted, hence the skipped frames; GPU threads are skipped.
Reports `FrameId` and `FrameAbsoluteId` and gives a normal average per scope, but has no separate top five for normal frames.
Disposes after a `pcall` and reads stack-element views before the next fetch, but `Configure` runs outside the `pcall`, and it calls `FetchGroupDesc` without checking for group ID 0.
Returns `Report`; only the new file changed; all checks pass.

strengths: Correct per-level child-time accounting for self time
Splits scopes at frame boundaries correctly, including enters from before the snapshot
Gives a top five for normal frames and a normal average for each slow-frame scope
weaknesses: The `Configure` call on the iterator could have been checked more defensively, though it is inside the `pcall`
Can call `FetchTimerDesc` on unusual timer IDs, though it guards against timer ID 0

strengths: Checks the slot number and session validity
Takes care to read views before fetching the next one
weaknesses: Skips frames right after a capture pause and the first frame, so it may miss slow frames
No top five for normal frames
`Configure` runs outside the `pcall`, so the iterator can leak if it errors
